title: Swaziland
capsule: The territory of Swaziland came under British protection by an 1881 convention with the South African Republic (Transvaal), reflecting post-Zulu War regional diplomacy; a joint Transvaal-British administration (1890–1894) gave way to sole British High Commission administration in 1903 following the South African War. The Swazi royal house, consolidated by Sobhuza I (to 1836) and put under severe concession pressure during Mbandzeni's reign (1875–1889), retained its monarchical institutions under indirect rule while losing effective control of much of the territory's economic resources to European settlers. The period 1885–1908 marks the colonial demarcation phase; Swaziland remained a British protectorate outside the Union of South Africa until it became an independent kingdom under Sobhuza II on 6 September 1968, renamed Eswatini in 2018 by King Mswati III.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Colonial-era boundaries were formally surveyed and delimited; the protectorate's extent is well documented and essentially identical to the present state, though pre-colonial Swazi territorial claims before 1881 are less precisely defined.
